first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ, indicating friction in the user journey itself rather than acquisition or conversion strategy. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrated that reducing friction in early flows (signup simplification and onboarding shortening) drive measurable lifts in activation and completion. Verifying these provides concrete evidence of mechanism. While competitor pricing pressure is real, competing primarily on price with established SMB segments risks margin erosion and long-term unit economics. A simplify_onboarding experiment targets the immediate metrics degradation (activation down 6%, completion down 4%) and aligns with proven levers. Memory_91 shows activation messaging also works, but onboarding friction reduction has dual evidence and addresses both the activation and completion declines simultaneously. This preserves optionality on promotional pricing as a follow-up if the onboarding lift proves insufficient for SMB retention under competitive pressure.

final.rationale: Verified records show simplify_onboarding produced +13% completion lift and +3% retention gain (exp_86), addressing both the 4% completion decline and supporting long-term revenue quality. Signup simplification added +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB (exp_31), directly countering the 6% activation drop. Combined evidence is strong: two independent experiments show both mechanisms work, completion improvement drives retention gain (critical for sustainable revenue), and SMB activation lift offsets competitor pressure without requiring margin-destructive pricing. The -1% retention risk from signup simplification is offset by the +3% retention from onboarding shortening. This experiment addresses root friction rather than competing on price, preserving margin and long-term unit economics while immediately improving both reported metric declines. Standard scale allows learning curve validation before broad rollout.
